teaching_point: Dimple (Fitzpatrick) sign: lateral pinch makes the lesion dip below the surface because it is tethered to the dermis.
licence_note: DermNet image licence: https://dermnetnz.org/image-licence (watermarked low-res; personal/educational use with attribution)
attribution: Image: DermNet — Pinch sign of dermatofibroma (© DermNet) — https://dermnetnz.org/topics/dermatofibroma

teaching_point: Typical firm, pink-brown dome-shaped papule on a limb in an adult.
licence_note: DermNet image licence: https://dermnetnz.org/image-licence (watermarked low-res; personal/educational use with attribution)
attribution: Image: DermNet — Dermatofibroma (© Raimo Suhonen) — https://dermnetnz.org/topics/dermatofibroma

teaching_point: Dermoscopy: fine peripheral pigment network around a central white scar-like patch. This is the classic DF pattern; dermoscopy is supportive, not diagnostic.
dermnet_caption: Dermoscopy. Peripheral network, central white area: dermatofibroma
licence_note: DermNet image licence: https://dermnetnz.org/image-licence (watermarked low-res; personal/educational use with attribution)
attribution: Image: DermNet — Dermoscopy. Peripheral network, central white area: dermatofibroma (© DermNet) — https://dermnetnz.org/topics/dermatofibroma-images

teaching_point: Dermoscopy variant with a prominent central white area. Atypical or asymmetric patterns need a biopsy to exclude melanoma (DF can mimic it).
dermnet_caption: Dermoscopy. Prominent central white area: dermatofibroma
licence_note: DermNet image licence: https://dermnetnz.org/image-licence (watermarked low-res; personal/educational use with attribution)
attribution: Image: DermNet — Dermoscopy. Prominent central white area: dermatofibroma (© DermNet) — https://dermnetnz.org/topics/dermatofibroma-images

teaching_point: DFSP early: ill-defined, firm pink-brown plaque on the trunk, easily dismissed as a scar or DF.
licence_note: DermNet image licence: https://dermnetnz.org/image-licence (watermarked low-res; personal/educational use with attribution)
attribution: Image: DermNet — Lesion in 2014 (© DermNet) — https://dermnetnz.org/topics/dermatofibrosarcoma-protuberans

teaching_point: The same lesion one year later, now enlarging. A slowly growing indurated plaque or nodule needs referral (NG12 has no DFSP-specific rule, so refer urgently/through the local skin cancer route if concerned).
licence_note: DermNet image licence: https://dermnetnz.org/image-licence (watermarked low-res; personal/educational use with attribution)
attribution: Image: DermNet — Same lesion in 2015 (© DermNet) — https://dermnetnz.org/topics/dermatofibrosarcoma-protuberans

teaching_point: Hairless yellow-orange scalp plaque in a child. Thickens and becomes verrucous at puberty.
dermnet_caption: A hairless occipital patch in a child - the nevus sebaceous may become thicker and verrucous at puberty
licence_note: DermNet image licence: https://dermnetnz.org/image-licence (watermarked low-res; personal/educational use with attribution)
attribution: Image: DermNet — A hairless occipital patch in a child - the nevus sebaceous may become thicker and verrucous at puberty (© DermNet) — https://dermnetnz.org/topics/sebaceous-naevus

teaching_point: Long-standing naevus that has become rough and developed a benign cyst. Most secondary tumours are benign (trichoblastoma, syringocystadenoma papilliferum).
dermnet_caption: Nevus sebaceous, present since birth, slowly become rough and has developed a benign cyst within it
licence_note: DermNet image licence: https://dermnetnz.org/image-licence (watermarked low-res; personal/educational use with attribution)
attribution: Image: DermNet — Nevus sebaceous, present since birth, slowly become rough and has developed a benign cyst within it (© DermNet) — https://dermnetnz.org/topics/sebaceous-naevus

teaching_point: Sebaceous naevus in skin of colour: the yellow colour is hard to see, so the clue is a congenital hairless plaque.
dermnet_caption: A nevus sebaceous in skin of colour - the typical yellow colour cannot be appreciated in darker skin types
licence_note: DermNet image licence: https://dermnetnz.org/image-licence (watermarked low-res; personal/educational use with attribution)
attribution: Image: DermNet — A nevus sebaceous in skin of colour - the typical yellow colour cannot be appreciated in darker skin types (© Dr Richard Ashton) — https://dermnetnz.org/topics/sebaceous-naevus

teaching_point: New crusted nodule at the edge of a sebaceous naevus. Any new nodule, ulcer or bleeding within a naevus needs referral for biopsy (BCC risk is under 1%).
dermnet_caption: A crusted area has developed at the edge of this nevus sebaceous - biopsy is needed to exclude either a benign or malignant lesion arising within
licence_note: DermNet image licence: https://dermnetnz.org/image-licence (watermarked low-res; personal/educational use with attribution)
attribution: Image: DermNet — A crusted area has developed at the edge of this nevus sebaceous - biopsy is needed to exclude either a benign or malignant lesion arising within (© DermNet) — https://dermnetnz.org/topics/sebaceous-naevus

teaching_point: Palpating an epidermoid cyst accentuates the central punctum.
dermnet_caption: Palpating an epidermoid cyst - note this accentuates the punctum
licence_note: DermNet image licence: https://dermnetnz.org/image-licence (watermarked low-res; personal/educational use with attribution)
attribution: Image: DermNet — Palpating an epidermoid cyst - note this accentuates the punctum (© DermNet) — https://dermnetnz.org/topics/epidermoid-cyst

teaching_point: Recurrence beside a previous scar: the cyst wall was left behind. Complete removal of the wall prevents recurrence.
dermnet_caption: A recurrent epidermoid cyst - note the scar from a previous incomplete excision
licence_note: DermNet image licence: https://dermnetnz.org/image-licence (watermarked low-res; personal/educational use with attribution)
attribution: Image: DermNet — A recurrent epidermoid cyst - note the scar from a previous incomplete excision (© DermNet) — https://dermnetnz.org/topics/epidermoid-cyst

teaching_point: Multiple facial epidermoid cysts in Gardner syndrome (APC/FAP variant). Multiple or early-onset cysts plus a bowel family history should trigger GP referral to genetics/colorectal.
dermnet_caption: Multiple facial epidermal cysts in Gardner syndrome
licence_note: DermNet image licence: https://dermnetnz.org/image-licence (watermarked low-res; personal/educational use with attribution)
attribution: Image: DermNet — Multiple facial epidermal cysts in Gardner syndrome (© DermNet) — https://dermnetnz.org/topics/gardner-syndrome

teaching_point: Scalp osteoma in Gardner syndrome: a bony-hard, fixed lump. Osteomas, dental anomalies and desmoids are part of the syndrome.
dermnet_caption: A scalp osteoma in Gardner syndrome
licence_note: DermNet image licence: https://dermnetnz.org/image-licence (watermarked low-res; personal/educational use with attribution)
attribution: Image: DermNet — A scalp osteoma in Gardner syndrome (© Dr Lawrence Meyerson) — https://dermnetnz.org/images/gardner-syndrome-images

teaching_point: Pilar (trichilemmal) cyst on the scalp: smooth, firm, no punctum. This is the main scalp DDx of an epidermoid cyst.
licence_note: DermNet image licence: https://dermnetnz.org/image-licence (watermarked low-res; personal/educational use with attribution)
attribution: Image: DermNet — Pilar cyst (© DermNet) — https://dermnetnz.org/topics/cutaneous-cysts-and-pseudocysts

teaching_point: Soft, mobile subcutaneous lipoma on the back. Multiple painful lipomas in an older woman with obesity and low mood suggest Dercum disease.
dermnet_caption: A typical lipoma on the back
licence_note: DermNet image licence: https://dermnetnz.org/image-licence (watermarked low-res; personal/educational use with attribution)
attribution: Image: DermNet — A typical lipoma on the back (© DermNet) — https://dermnetnz.org/topics/lipoma

teaching_point: Pyogenic granuloma on the lip: rapidly growing, friable, bleeds easily. It needs histology after removal because amelanotic melanoma can mimic it.
licence_note: DermNet image licence: https://dermnetnz.org/image-licence (watermarked low-res; personal/educational use with attribution)
attribution: Image: DermNet — Pyogenic granuloma (© DermNet) — https://dermnetnz.org/topics/pyogenic-granuloma

teaching_point: Pedunculated PG on the lower eyelid. Periocular site, so refer rather than treat in primary care.
licence_note: DermNet image licence: https://dermnetnz.org/image-licence (watermarked low-res; personal/educational use with attribution)
attribution: Image: DermNet — Pyogenic granuloma (© DermNet) — https://dermnetnz.org/topics/pyogenic-granuloma

teaching_point: Angiokeratoma circumscriptum: a congenital band of dark red warty papules on a limb (one of the five variants).
licence_note: DermNet image licence: https://dermnetnz.org/image-licence (watermarked low-res; personal/educational use with attribution)
attribution: Image: DermNet — Angiokeratoma circumscriptum (© DermNet) — https://dermnetnz.org/topics/angiokeratoma

teaching_point: Angiokeratoma of Fordyce on the scrotum: common, benign, age-related. Reassure unless bleeding.
licence_note: DermNet image licence: https://dermnetnz.org/image-licence (watermarked low-res; personal/educational use with attribution)
attribution: Image: DermNet — Angiokeratoma of Fordyce on scrotum (© DermNet) — https://dermnetnz.org/topics/angiokeratoma

teaching_point: Solitary dark angiokeratoma. A black papule can mimic nodular melanoma, so refer if any doubt (dermoscopy shows red-blue lacunae).
licence_note: DermNet image licence: https://dermnetnz.org/image-licence (watermarked low-res; personal/educational use with attribution)
attribution: Image: DermNet — Angiokeratoma (© DermNet) — https://dermnetnz.org/topics/angiokeratoma-images

teaching_point: Multiple small angiokeratomas in suspected Fabry disease (angiokeratoma corporis diffusum). Ask about burning hand/foot pain, reduced sweating, renal and cardiac problems; GP referral for alpha-galactosidase A testing.
licence_note: DermNet image licence: https://dermnetnz.org/image-licence (watermarked low-res; personal/educational use with attribution)
attribution: Image: DermNet — Angiokeratomas in suspected Fabry disease (© DermNet) — https://dermnetnz.org/topics/angiokeratoma-images

teaching_point: Soft, skin-coloured neurofibroma with the 'buttonhole' sign (invaginates on pressure). Solitary lesions are common and not necessarily NF1.
licence_note: DermNet image licence: https://dermnetnz.org/image-licence (watermarked low-res; personal/educational use with attribution)
attribution: Image: DermNet — Neurofibroma (© DermNet) — https://dermnetnz.org/topics/neurofibromatosis

teaching_point: Plexiform neurofibroma: a large, soft, 'bag of worms' pigmented mass, characteristic of NF1. New pain, rapid growth or hardening means urgent referral (MPNST risk).
licence_note: DermNet image licence: https://dermnetnz.org/image-licence (watermarked low-res; personal/educational use with attribution)
attribution: Image: DermNet — Plexiform neurofibroma (© DermNet) — https://dermnetnz.org/topics/neurofibromatosis

teaching_point: Pilomatricoma: a hard, sometimes faceted or bluish papule in a child or teenager (head, neck, arm). Excised by specialists.
licence_note: DermNet image licence: https://dermnetnz.org/image-licence (watermarked low-res; personal/educational use with attribution)
attribution: Image: DermNet — Pilomatricoma (© DermNet) — https://dermnetnz.org/topics/pilomatricoma

teaching_point: Digital myxoid pseudocyst: a shiny translucent papule over the distal interphalangeal joint or proximal nail fold, often with a nail groove. Linked to osteoarthritis.
licence_note: DermNet image licence: https://dermnetnz.org/image-licence (watermarked low-res; personal/educational use with attribution)
attribution: Image: DermNet — Myxoid cyst (© DermNet) — https://dermnetnz.org/topics/digital-myxoid-pseudocyst

teaching_point: Sebaceous hyperplasia: yellowish umbilicated facial papules, often multiple. The main DDx is early nodular BCC (BCC is pearly with arborising vessels, not lobular yellow).
licence_note: DermNet image licence: https://dermnetnz.org/image-licence (watermarked low-res; personal/educational use with attribution)
attribution: Image: DermNet — Sebaceous hyperplasia (© DermNet) — https://dermnetnz.org/topics/sebaceous-hyperplasia

teaching_point: Linear morphoea (limb). En coup de sabre is the frontal-scalp form of this condition. Refer: it may need systemic treatment to limit growth and atrophy problems.
licence_note: DermNet image licence: https://dermnetnz.org/image-licence (watermarked low-res; personal/educational use with attribution)
attribution: Image: DermNet — Morphoea (© DermNet) — https://dermnetnz.org/topics/morphoea
